title: Temperature and enzyme activity
caption: Below the optimum the rate roughly doubles for every 10 °C rise, as molecules gain kinetic energy and collide more often. Beyond the optimum, about 37 °C for human enzymes, hydrogen bonds break, the active site changes shape and the enzyme denatures: the rate collapses.
alt: A curve of relative enzyme activity against temperature that rises steadily from 20 degrees, peaks at 37 degrees and then falls steeply to almost nothing by 50 degrees.
description: From 20 °C to 37 °C the rate rises steadily, roughly doubling for each 10 °C.
The peak, the optimum, is at about 37 °C for a human enzyme.
Above the optimum the enzyme denatures and the rate falls steeply.
By 50 °C almost no active enzyme is left.
